scenes.headline: How an encoder picks from a list
scenes.sub: GLiNER2.5-Decide writes the labels into its own input.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Meadow! This model picks from any list of labels without writing a word. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Each label becomes a marker token in the same sequence as the text, and a small head scores every marker. The options are tokens too.
scenes.say: Each label becomes a marker token in the same sequence as the text, and a small head scores every marker.

scenes.title: One pass, one score per label

steps.say: Every label is written into the input behind its own marker token. Then comes the text.
One encoder reads it all at once, both ways. The text reads the labels, and the labels read the text.
Each marker's final state goes through a small two-layer head and comes out as one number.

steps.note: two labels or twenty-eight: no weight changes shape
steps.say: A softmax across those numbers gives the answer. Two labels or twenty-eight, no weight changes shape.

steps.label: Per-option scorer: each option alone
steps.say: Some decision models score each option alone, so the order of the list can't matter.

steps.label: Kev: one shared sequence, left to right
steps.say: Kev reads its options left to right. Each one sees the ones before it.

steps.label: GLiNER2.5-Decide: everything reads everything
steps.say: Here, every label reads every other label and the text. So order, and other questions in the call, are input too.

scenes.title: The card's email: how likely is critical?
scenes.note: same email; with the route head, critical beats high
scenes.say: I measured the card's own email. Alone, urgency comes back high. Add two more questions, and it says critical.

steps.say: This is the interface: a schema of typed questions, each with its choices.
Out comes one choice per question. Behind the picture, both questions share one sequence with the text.

scenes.title: Fast Decisions, public split
scenes.note: model score reported by FluidInference; floors computed from the same rows
scenes.say: On the public split it scores about sixty-three percent. Guessing gets twenty; the most common answer, twenty-six.

scenes.text: Putting the labels in the sequence lets one encoder make any decision, and makes the list itself part of the input.
scenes.mark: the list itself part of the input
scenes.say: Labels in the sequence let one small encoder make any decision, and make the list part of the input.

recap: Labels become marker tokens in the input
A small head scores each marker
Order and other heads can move the answer
scenes.say: Labels become tokens, a small head scores each one, and the rest of the schema can move the answer.
